title: A Path a Car Can Drive: Searching Over Pose and Heading With Arcs the Car Can Make, and Why the Grid Path With Its Corners Is Not a Path at All

questions.question: Why is a path through the cells of a grid not a path for a car?
options: Its cells are larger than the car
It has corners, which need a curvature no car has
A grid path is longer than it need be
It ignores the cost of the cells
questions.explanation: A grid path turns through a right angle between neighbouring cells. A car turns along an arc no tighter than its smallest circle.

questions.question: The hybrid path had a largest curvature of:
options: 1.35 per metre, within the limit of 1.35
15.7 per metre, as for the grid path
0.74 per metre
2.50 per metre, a little over the limit
questions.explanation: The path is a chain of arcs of the bicycle model, each steered no harder than the car can, so its curvature is at most the limit of 1.35.

questions.question: The corner of the grid path needed a curvature of:
options: 1.35 per metre, the car's limit
15.7 per metre
7.1 per metre
0 per metre: a corner has no curvature
questions.explanation: A quarter turn, 1.57 rad, between two poses 0.1 m apart is 15.7 per metre, more than ten times what the car can do.

questions.question: A goal that was walled in was reported as:
options: Not found, with an empty path
Found, at the nearest free pose
Found, by a path through the wall
Still searching when the test ended
questions.explanation: After the limit of 4000 expansions the planner returned an empty path and said not found. Returning the nearest pose would send the car to a wall.

questions.question: What keeps the search from running for ever over continuous poses?
options: The arcs have a fixed length
The heuristic never overestimates
Nodes are kept one to a cell of a coarse grid of position and heading
The penalty for reversing
questions.explanation: A new pose that lands in a cell of position and heading already reached more cheaply is dropped, so the number of nodes is bounded by the number of cells.

questions.question: What does a finer grid of headings cost?
options: A less accurate final heading
Longer arcs
Nothing: the search is the same size
More expansions: 1146 at 12 headings and 2675 at 48
questions.explanation: More headings to a cell means more distinct nodes to expand. The search grew from 1146 expansions to 2675.
